Context information about the ServiceNow change request * @param {string} inputs.context.url - The URL of the change request in Service Operations Workspace * @param {string} inputs.context.table - The ServiceNow table name (e.g., 'change_request') * @param {string} inputs.context.record_sys_id - agent_id: The agent id. * - context: An object that carries additional contextual information for the agent. * It always includes a "pageContext" and may include a "triggerContext", * depending on how and from where the agent is invoked. * * Behavior by invocation type: * --------------------------------- * - When invoked via the startAiAgentConversation API: * If a "contextMemory" parameter is provided in the API request, * it will be available here as the "triggerContext". * The "pageContext" is always present in this call, regardless * of whether the agent is executed individually or as part of a use case. * Example: * { * pageContext: { ... }, * triggerContext: { ... } // Derived from contextMemory (if passed) * } * * - When invoked as part of a use case or workflow: * The "pageContext" and "triggerContext" objects available here * may have been *modified* by the use case’s context processing script. * This means the use case may alter, extend, or overwrite values * from the original "pageContext" or "triggerContext" * before the context reaches the agent. * If the use case was originally triggered via the API, * the initial "triggerContext" is still derived from the * "contextMemory" parameter, but its contents may have been updated * by the use case logic. * * - When executed directly (standalone agent execution): * The "pageContext" will always be present (default or empty), * and the "triggerContext" will only be populated if explicitly * passed through the API call. * Return an modified context like: { pageContext : {},triggerContext:{} } */ (function(task, user_utterance, agent_id, context) { return { pageContext : context?.pageContext, triggerContext : context?.triggerContext }; })(task,user_utterance, agent_id, context);]]></context_processing_script><description>The primary purpose of this agent is to review logs of a specified instance or application / plug-in upgrade in ServiceNow, classify them by priority, review the skipped upgrades and then suggest best-practice actions against these skipped upgrades based on deep analysis of changes.</description><extends/><extension_configuration/><external_agent_configuration/><inputs>{}</inputs><instructions>#STEPS:
##INITIALISATION
1. First, politely greet the user and ask them which upgrade they need assistance with today. Retrieve the list of the last 3 upgrades in the system using the "Retrieve Latest Upgrades" tool, PRESENT them to the user in a simple, comprehensible format, and ASK them which one they need help with.
2. a.IF the user responds with one of the three upgrades listed, proceed to step 2b. ELSE IF user says their tool is not listed OR they specify a different upgrade name in their response, JUMP to step 3. b. Retrieve additional details regarding the upgrade using the "Retrieve Upgrade History Record Details" tool using the sys ID of the upgrade record retrieved from the previous step as the input. c. Store the output of this upgrade in the <selected_upgrade_record> variable in your memory and THEN proceed to the UPGRADE ANALYSIS section.
3. IF the user responds that their upgrade is not listed or requests for a different upgrade or specifies a different upgrade name, enter the CLARIFICATION LOOP.
##CLARIFICATION LOOP
1. ASK the user specify the exact name of the upgrade they are looking to review IF they have not already done so. Ask them to be as accurate as possible as this would help you search for the upgrade history record much quicker. State sample format to help them understand, like "Suite Install for Now Assist Admin Console 28.9.20260505". Once the user confirms the name, proceed to step 2.
2. a. IF the user provided the name of the plugin/app/instance upgrade (For eg., "Suite Install for Now Assist Admin Console 28.9.20260505"), directly jump to step 3. 2. b. ELSE IF the user asked a question, or does not know the name of the plugin, ask them to navigate to the Upgrade History [sys_upgrade_history] record, find their upgrade, and send to you the "To" field value.
3. Once you receive a valid plugin/app/instance upgrade name, attempt to retrieve the related record from the Upgrade History table using the tool "Retrieve Upgrade History Record" using the name as the input to the tool. Store the output of this upgrade in the <selected_upgrade_record> variable in your memory
4. IF you are able to successfully retrieve the record, present the information to the user and ask for their confirmation whether this is the upgrade they implied. If they confirm, proceed to UPGRADE ANALYSIS, else proceed to CLOSE EXECUTION
##UPGRADE ANALYSIS
1. Once the user confirms which upgrade they need assistance with, generate a summary of the upgrade record using the "Analyze Skipped Upgrades (Summary)" tool which takes the sys ID of the upgrade record generated above as the input and provides a count of skipped upgrades by priority 2. Present the output, which would be a list of skipped record count by priority, to the user in a cleanly formatted, comprehensible manner. 3. If the output contains Priority 1 or 2, inform the user that for those skipped records, manual action need to be taken and you are not equipped to assist there. Present the user with the other priority options (that are not 1 or 2) available based on the output from step 2. (include ones with priority empty, if they are present in the output) 4. If the user responds with a valid priority number between 3 and 5, proceed to the SKIPPED UPGRADE ANALYSIS phase.
##SKIPPED UPGRADE ANALYSIS
1. Using the "Retrieve Skipped Upgrades by Priority" tool, with the inputs of the upgrade_id retrieved from step 1 of the UPGRADE ANALYSIS phase and the priority number (make sure you ONLY extract the priority number as the input, and not the string containing the term "priority") user specified in Step 4 of the UPGRADE ANALYSIS phase, retrieve the list of skipped upgrades 2. The output from the above step would be in a JSON format, you MUST present this to the user in a clean list format, with ONLY the sub-headers: Name, File Name, Disposition, Skip Reason & Comments. (The list should have a numerical count starting from 1, the value for each sub-header should be extracted from the output JSON. Do NOT include the sys ID but store it to your memory for each of the skipped upgrade listed in the corresponding list number), along with a message stating that these are the first 5 skipped upgrade files found and ASK which skipped upgrade they would like to take action on. They can either specify the corresponding number or the name of the skipped upgrade file. Wait for user input. 3. If the user responds with a valid number or skipped upgrade name, retrieve the corresponding sys ID of the skipped upgrade and use that as an input to the 'Compare with Previous Version' tool and read the output JSON 4. IF the output from the above step is NOT along the lines of "no old version found", extract the "Differences" key of the JSON and present it to the user in a clean, comprehensible format - highlighting what was added/removed, in which field (which would be the last term in the path value) and what was the old value and what would be the new value. 5. IF the output WAS along the lines of "no old version found", then simply review the skipped upgrade file output from the output from Step 3 and present its summary to the user.
## CLOSE EXECUTION
1. IF you were able to successfully retrieve the upgrade history record, review the skipped upgrades and suggest actions to the user, politely thank the user and let them know you were glad to help them. Terminate the execution.
2. ELSE IF you were unable to successfully retrieve the upgrade history record OR review the skipped upgrades OR suggest actions to the user, apologize to the user for not being able to assist further and present them with a link to the skipped upgrade record for manual analysis</instructions><internal_name>global.x_snc_ai_upgrade_0.Post Upgrade Analysis Agent</internal_name><name>Post Upgrade Analysis Agent</name><outputs>""</outputs><parent/><post_processing_message/><processing_message>Initiating Post-Upgrade Analysis Agent</processing_message><proficiency>- Expert in post-upgrade analysis for ServiceNow instances, applications, and plug-ins, with specialized skills in reviewing upgrade logs, classifying skipped upgrades by priority, and providing actionable recommendations based on best-practice guidelines and deep change analysis. Capable of guiding users through complex upgrade review processes, ensuring skipped upgrades are properly understood and addressed. - Able to retrieve and present the last three upgrades from the ServiceNow upgrade history, facilitating user selection and ensuring the agent can focus analysis on the most relevant upgrade events. - Capable of retrieving comprehensive details for a selected upgrade history record, enabling thorough review and contextual analysis of upgrade outcomes, including skipped upgrades and their implications. - <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_script_include"><sys_script_include action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><access>public</access><active>true</active><api_name>global.VersionPayloadXmlComparator</api_name><caller_access/><client_callable>false</client_callable><description>This is used by the Post Upgrade Analyses AI Agent</description><mobile_callable>false</mobile_callable><name>VersionPayloadXmlComparator</name><sandbox_callable>false</sandbox_callable><script><![CDATA[var VersionPayloadXmlComparator = Class.create();
VersionPayloadXmlComparator.prototype = {
        initialize: function() {},

        /**
         * Compare the payload XML from two sys_update_version records.
         *
         * @param {String} oldVersionSysId - sys_id of the older version record
         * @param {String} newVersionSysId - sys_id of the newer/current version record
         * @returns {Object} Comparison result
         */
        compare: function(newVersionSysId) {
            //this._validateSysId(oldVersionSysId, 'oldVersionSysId');
            this._validateSysId(newVersionSysId, 'newVersionSysId');

            var newVersion = this._getVersion(newVersionSysId);
			var oldVersion = this._getOldVersion(newVersionSysId);

			if(oldVersion == "not found")
				return "No old version found";

			var oldVersionSysId = oldVersion.sys_id.toString();
            var oldXml = oldVersion.getValue('payload') || '';
            var newXml = newVersion.getValue('payload') || '';

            this._validateXml(oldXml, oldVersionSysId);
            this._validateXml(newXml, newVersionSysId);

            var oldValues = this._flattenXml(oldXml);
            var newValues = this._flattenXml(newXml);

            var result = {
                old_version: {
                    sys_id: oldVersionSysId,
                    record_name: oldVersion.getDisplayValue('file_name'),
                    state: oldVersion.resolution_status.getDisplayValue(),
					disposition: oldVersion.diposition.getDisplayValue(),
                    updated_on: oldVersion.getValue('sys_updated_on')
                },
                new_version: {
                    sys_id: newVersionSysId,
                    record_name: newVersion.getDisplayValue('file_name'),
                    state: newVersion.resolution_status.getDisplayValue(),
					disposition: newVersion.diposition.getDisplayValue(),
                    updated_on: newVersion.getValue('sys_updated_on')
                },
                summary: {
                    added: 0,
                    removed: 0,
                    modified: 0,
                    unchanged: 0,
                    total_differences: 0
                },
                differences: []
            };

            var path;
            var seen = {};

            // Nodes/attributes removed or modified
            for (path in oldValues) {
                if (!oldValues.hasOwnProperty(path)) {
                    continue;
                }

                seen[path] = true;

                if (!newValues.hasOwnProperty(path)) {
                    result.differences.push({
                        type: 'removed',
                        path: path,
                        old_value: oldValues[path],
                        new_value: null
                    });
                    result.summary.removed++;
                } else if (oldValues[path] !== newValues[path]) {
                    result.differences.push({
                        type: 'modified',
                        path: path,
                        old_value: oldValues[path],
                        new_value: newValues[path]
                    });
                    result.summary.modified++;
                } else {
                    result.summary.unchanged++;
                }
            }

            // Nodes/attributes added
            for (path in newValues) {
                if (!newValues.hasOwnProperty(path) || seen[path]) {
                    continue;
                }

                result.differences.push({
                    type: 'added',
                    path: path,
                    old_value: null,
                    new_value: newValues[path]
                });
                result.summary.added++;
            }

            result.summary.total_differences =
                result.summary.added +
                result.summary.removed +
                result.summary.modified;

            return result;
        },

        /**
         * Gets a sys_update_version record.
         */
        _getVersion: function(sysId) {
            var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_upgrade_history_log');
            if (!gr.get(sysId)) {
                throw new Error('Version record not found: ' + sysId);
            }

            if (!gr.canRead()) {
                throw new Error('Not authorized to read version record: ' + sysId);
            }

            return gr;
        },

        _getOldVersion: function(currentVersion) {
                var skp = new GlideRecord('sys_upgrade_history_log');
                if (skp.get(currentVersion.toString())) {
                    var getPrevSkp = new GlideRecord('sys_upgrade_history_log');
                    getPrevSkp.addQuery("disposition", "4");
                    getPrevSkp.addQuery("changed", "true");
                    getPrevSkp.addQuery("file_name", skp.getValue('file_name'));
                    getPrevSkp.addQuery("sys_created_on", "<", skp.sys_created_on);
                    getPrevSkp.orderByDesc("sys_created_on");
                    getPrevSkp.query();
                    if (getPrevSkp.next()) {
							return getPrevSkp;
                    }
					else
						return "not found";
				}
		},

                    /**
                     * Validates XML prior to parsing.
                     */
                    _validateXml: function(xml, versionSysId) {
                            if (!xml) {
                                throw new Error('Payload is empty for version record: ' + versionSysId);
                            }

                            xml = GlideXMLUtil.removeInvalidChars(xml);

                            var validationError = GlideXMLUtil.validateXML(xml, false, false);
                            if (validationError) {
                                throw new Error(
                                    'Invalid XML payload for version record ' +
                                    versionSysId +
                                    ': ' +
                                    validationError
                                );
                            }
                        },

                        /**
                         * Converts XML into a path/value map for comparison.
                         *
                         * Examples:
                         * /sys_script/name = "My Business Rule"
                         * /sys_script/active = "true"
                         * /sys_script/script = "..."
                         * /sys_script@action_insert = "true"
                         */
                        _flattenXml: function(xml) {
                            var document = new XMLDocument2();
                            document.parseXML(GlideXMLUtil.removeInvalidChars(xml));

                            var root = document.getDocumentElement();
                            var values = {};

                            this._walkNode(root, '/' + root.getNodeName(), values);

                            return values;
                        },

                        /**
                         * Recursively walks XML elements and collects values and attributes.
                         * Element indexes make repeated nodes distinguishable.
                         */
                        _walkNode: function(node, path, values) {
                            var attributes = node.getAttributes();
                            var attributeName;

                            // Add attributes
                            for (attributeName in attributes) {
                                if (attributes.hasOwnProperty(attributeName)) {
                                    values[path + '/@' + attributeName] = String(attributes[attributeName]);
                                }
                            }

                            var iterator = node.getChildNodeIterator();
                            var children = [];
                            var nameCounts = {};
                            var child;

                            // Ignore whitespace-only #text nodes introduced by formatted XML.
                            while (iterator.hasNext()) {
                                child = iterator.next();

                                if (child.getNodeName() === '#text') {
                                    var text = String(child.getNodeValue() || '').replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, '');
                                    if (text) {
                                        values[path] = text;
                                    }
                                    continue;
                                }

                                children.push(child);
                                nameCounts[child.getNodeName()] = (nameCounts[child.getNodeName()] || 0) + 1;
                            }

                            // Add children. Index only repeated sibling element names.
                            var nameIndexes = {};
                            for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                                child = children[i];

                                var childName = child.getNodeName();
                                nameIndexes[childName] = (nameIndexes[childName] || 0) + 1;

                                var childPath = path + '/' + childName;
                                if (nameCounts[childName] > 1) {
                                    childPath += '[' + nameIndexes[childName] + ']';
                                }

                                this._walkNode(child, childPath, values);
                            }
                        },

                        _validateSysId: function(sysId, parameterName) {
                            if (!sysId || !/^[0-9a-f]{32}$/i.test(String(sysId))) {
                                throw new Error(parameterName + ' must be a valid 32-character sys_id.');
                            }
                        },

                        type: 'VersionPayloadXmlComparator'
                };]]></script><sys_class_name>sys_script_include</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>sharath.vasishta@snc</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-14 06:00:40</sys_created_on><sys_id>a3482fbdc31b0f1040829a4bb0013183</sys_id><sys_mod_count>7</sys_mod_count><sys_name>VersionPayloadXmlComparator</sys_name><sys_package display_value="Global" source="global">global</sys_package><sys_policy>read</sys_policy><sys_scope display_value="Global">global</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_script_include_a3482fbdc31b0f1040829a4bb0013183</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>sharath.vasishta@snc</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-16 05:39:40</sys_updated_on></sys_script_include></record_update>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update sys_domain="global" table="sn_aia_version"><sn_aia_version action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><condition/><instructions>#STEPS:
##INITIALISATION
1. First, politely greet the user and ask them which upgrade they need assistance with today. Retrieve the list of the last 3 upgrades in the system using the "Retrieve Latest Upgrades" tool, PRESENT them to the user in a simple, comprehensible format, and ASK them which one they need help with.
2. a.IF the user responds with one of the three upgrades listed, proceed to step 2b. ELSE IF user says their tool is not listed OR they specify a different upgrade name in their response, JUMP to step 3. b. Retrieve additional details regarding the upgrade using the "Retrieve Upgrade History Record Details" tool using the sys ID of the upgrade record retrieved from the previous step as the input. c. Store the output of this upgrade in the <selected_upgrade_record> variable in your memory and THEN proceed to the UPGRADE ANALYSIS section.
3. IF the user responds that their upgrade is not listed or requests for a different upgrade or specifies a different upgrade name, enter the CLARIFICATION LOOP.
##CLARIFICATION LOOP
1. ASK the user specify the exact name of the upgrade they are looking to review IF they have not already done so. Ask them to be as accurate as possible as this would help you search for the upgrade history record much quicker. State sample format to help them understand, like "Suite Install for Now Assist Admin Console 28.9.20260505". Once the user confirms the name, proceed to step 2.
2. a. IF the user provided the name of the plugin/app/instance upgrade (For eg., "Suite Install for Now Assist Admin Console 28.9.20260505"), directly jump to step 3. 2. b. ELSE IF the user asked a question, or does not know the name of the plugin, ask them to navigate to the Upgrade History [sys_upgrade_history] record, find their upgrade, and send to you the "To" field value.
3. Once you receive a valid plugin/app/instance upgrade name, attempt to retrieve the related record from the Upgrade History table using the tool "Retrieve Upgrade History Record" using the name as the input to the tool. Store the output of this upgrade in the <selected_upgrade_record> variable in your memory
4. IF you are able to successfully retrieve the record, present the information to the user and ask for their confirmation whether this is the upgrade they implied. If they confirm, proceed to UPGRADE ANALYSIS, else proceed to CLOSE EXECUTION
##UPGRADE ANALYSIS
1. Once the user confirms which upgrade they need assistance with, generate a summary of the upgrade record using the "Analyze Skipped Upgrades (Summary)" tool which takes the sys ID of the upgrade record generated above as the input and provides a count of skipped upgrades by priority 2. Present the output, which would be a list of skipped record count by priority, to the user in a cleanly formatted, comprehensible manner. 3. If the output contains Priority 1 or 2, inform the user that for those skipped records, manual action need to be taken and you are not equipped to assist there. Present the user with the other priority options (that are not 1 or 2) available based on the output from step 2. (include ones with priority empty, if they are present in the output) 4. If the user responds with a valid priority number between 3 and 5, proceed to the SKIPPED UPGRADE ANALYSIS phase.
##SKIPPED UPGRADE ANALYSIS
1. Using the "Retrieve Skipped Upgrades by Priority" tool, with the inputs of the upgrade_id retrieved from step 1 of the UPGRADE ANALYSIS phase and the priority number (make sure you ONLY extract the priority number as the input, and not the string containing the term "priority") user specified in Step 4 of the UPGRADE ANALYSIS phase, retrieve the list of skipped upgrades 2. The output from the above step would be in a JSON format, you MUST present this to the user in a clean list format, with ONLY the sub-headers: Name, File Name, Disposition, Skip Reason & Comments. (The list should have a numerical count starting from 1, the value for each sub-header should be extracted from the output JSON. Do NOT include the sys ID but store it to your memory for each of the skipped upgrade listed in the corresponding list number), along with a message stating that these are the first 5 skipped upgrade files found and ASK which skipped upgrade they would like to take action on. They can either specify the corresponding number or the name of the skipped upgrade file. Wait for user input. 3. If the user responds with a valid number or skipped upgrade name, retrieve the corresponding sys ID of the skipped upgrade and use that as an input to the 'Compare with Previous Version' tool and read the output JSON 4. IF the output from the above step is NOT along the lines of "no old version found", extract the "Differences" key of the JSON and present it to the user in a clean, comprehensible format - highlighting what was added/removed, in which field (which would be the last term in the path value) and what was the old value and what would be the new value. 5. IF the output WAS along the lines of "no old version found", then simply review the skipped upgrade file output from the output from Step 3 and present its summary to the user.
## CLOSE EXECUTION
1. IF you were able to successfully retrieve the upgrade history record, review the skipped upgrades and suggest actions to the user, politely thank the user and let them know you were glad to help them. Terminate the execution.
2. ELSE IF you were unable to successfully retrieve the upgrade history record OR review the skipped upgrades OR suggest actions to the user, apologize to the user for not being able to assist further and present them with a link to the skipped upgrade record for manual analysis</instructions><state>published</state><sys_class_name>sn_aia_version</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>sharath.vasishta@snc</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-11 10:02:38</sys_created_on><sys_domain>global</sys_domain><sys_id>26e2c141c35f8f1040829a4bb0013110</sys_id><sys_mod_count>9</sys_mod_count><sys_name>V2</sys_name><sys_overrides/><sys_package display_value="AI Upgrade Monitor" source="x_snc_ai_upgrade_0">134b44d287924750602686e70cbb3543</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="AI Upgrade Monitor">134b44d287924750602686e70cbb3543</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sn_aia_version_26e2c141c35f8f1040829a4bb0013110</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>sharath.vasishta@snc</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-16 06:27:04</sys_updated_on><target_id>a2a916c5876ecb10a4bded360cbb350e</target_id><target_table>sn_aia_agent</target_table><version_name>V2</version_name><version_number>2</version_number></sn_aia_version></record_update>
